sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sugreev Kumar Sharma Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J.
Heard learned Counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State/respondent as well as perused the record.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed by the applicant apprehending his arrest in Case Crime No.470 of 2007 under Section 376/511 I.P.C. Police Station Rampur Kalan, District Sitapur.
In the prosecution case it is alleged that niece of the informant has been abducted by the accused and was kept for 5-6 hours at unknown place.
Later on she was found in unconscious state.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has no criminal history.
Charge-sheet was filed under Section 354 Indian penal Code in which he has been enlarged on bail by the learned court below.
The incident is of the year 2007.
Charge-sheet in this regard has been filed.
During investigation the applicant was not arrested.
The victim has not been subjected to the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim under section 161 Cr.P.C. is self contradictory.
The applicant has no criminal history.
There is no corroborative material in support of the prosecution case.
Learned Counsel for the applicant undertakes that the applicant shall cooperate in the trial.
He submits that recently the applicant has come to know that on 1.6.2024 non-bailable warrant has been issued against him.

Learned Addl. Government Advocate though has opposed the prayer of anticipatory bail, however,
he could not dispute the aforesaid facts.

On due consideration of the arguments advanced; perusal of the record; so also the fact that the applicant was not arrested during investigation, charge-sheet has been filed; he undertakes to cooperate in the trial and has cooperated in the investigation, it would be expedient in the interest of justice that the liberty of the applicant may be protected in view of dictum of Apex Court in re:
Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98.
Therefore, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.
